title: Most Disjoint Palindromes of Length at Least K
statement:
You get a string s and a number k. Pick some substrings of s so that:

  • each picked substring is a palindrome (it reads the same backwards),
  • each has length at least k,
  • no two of them overlap (they may sit right next to each other).

Return the largest number of substrings you can pick. Letters that are not in any picked substring are fine.

examples.why: "aa" + "aa". Picking the whole "aaaa" is a valid palindrome but counts only once, so shorter pieces win.
No odd palindrome of length 3 exists here, but the even one "abba" (length 4) does. Checking only length k would miss it.

hints: Let best[i] be the answer for the prefix s[0..i). Either the last letter is unused, or the prefix ends with a picked palindrome s[j..i).
With a table pal[j][i] telling whether s[j..i) is a palindrome, best[i] = max(best[i − 1], best[j] + 1 for every j ≤ i − k with s[j..i) a palindrome). That is O(n²).

You never need a palindrome longer than k + 1: any longer one contains, centred inside it, a palindrome of length k or k + 1 that ends earlier. So only check lengths k and k + 1 ending at each position, and take one greedily as soon as it fits.

explain.intuition:
A DP over prefixes always works: best[i] is the most pieces inside the first i letters. Either letter i − 1 is not used (best[i − 1]), or a picked palindrome s[j..i) ends there (best[j] + 1). A precomputed palindrome table makes each check O(1).

The key observation makes it much simpler. Strip one letter from each end of a palindrome and it is still a palindrome. So a long palindrome always contains a shorter one, of length exactly k or k + 1, centred inside it, which ends earlier. Ending earlier never hurts, because it leaves more room for the pieces after it. So scan left to right, and the first time a palindrome of length k or k + 1 ends inside the free part of the string, take it and continue after it.
steps: Set free = 0 (the first index not yet used) and count = 0.
For each end position i from 0 to n − 1:
If i − k + 1 ≥ free and s[i − k + 1 .. i] is a palindrome, or i − k ≥ free and s[i − k .. i] is a palindrome, then add 1 to count and set free = i + 1.
pitfalls: Checking only length k. Odd and even palindromes alternate, so "abba" with k = 3 needs length 4.
Greedily taking the longest palindrome at each point. In "aaaa" with k = 2 that gives 1 instead of 2.
Letting a new piece start before free, so two picks overlap.

solutions.title: Prefix DP with a palindrome table
solutions.idea: pal[j][i] says whether s[j..i] is a palindrome. best[i] is the most pieces in the first i letters: skip the last letter, or end a palindrome of length at least k there.

solutions.title: Greedy on lengths k and k + 1
solutions.idea: Any long palindrome contains a centred one of length k or k + 1 that ends earlier. Scan left to right and take the first such palindrome that fits in the free part.

followups: Return the chosen substrings, not just how many.
Each picked palindrome now scores its length. Maximise the total score. Does the k / k + 1 shortcut still hold?
